clue.text: Concentrate on replacing article in range

indicators.note: on replacing article says the word for on takes the place of the article inside the range

parts.note: a compass is a range or scope, as in 'within the compass of'
a is the indefinite article
re means on, concerning, as in business letters

explanation.surface: An instruction to focus on swapping out an item somewhere in a range, as if setting a test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concentrate' is a verb here, not the noun of an orange juice carton.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to squeeze something into less space is to make it denser or concentrated.

clue.text: Just after Thursday I will be very busy

parts.note: on can mean immediately after, as in 'on arrival' or 'on the hour'
the ego is the self, the I

explanation.surface: Someone warns that from Friday onwards they will be rushed off their feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a person constantly moving from task to task is extremely occupied.

clue.text: Ancient priest gets involved with choir

indicators.note: something involved is tangled up, so the letters of the two words are mixed together

explanation.surface: An elderly cleric starts singing with the church choir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ancient' looks like it describes the priest, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym in loose use: very old, dating from before written records.

clue.text: Steer clear of commercial breaks almost always

indicators.note: breaks means cuts into, so the commercial sits inside the shortened word
almost says the last letter of the word for always is dropped

parts.note: ever means always, as in 'ever hopeful'
an ad is a commercial

explanation.surface: A viewer's tactic of dodging the advert breaks nearly every time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'commercial breaks' reads as one phrase, the TV ad breaks; but 'breaks' is the container indicator acting on the commercial.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to dodge or avoid something is to keep away from it.

clue.text: Fellows in small river show sign of cold

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

indicators.note: in places the fellows within the other pieces

parts.note: the Nile is the great African river
F is an abbreviation for fellow, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Men standing in a little stream start showing they have caught a chill.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: sniffing repeatedly through a runny nose is a typical symptom of a head cold.

clue.text: Gold rush could be magnificent

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
a gust is a sudden rush of wind

explanation.surface: A gold rush might turn out to be a splendid thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'August' here is the adjective (stressed on the second syllable), not the month.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: august means grand, inspiring awe and respect.

clue.text: Illness stops a criminal obtaining wealth

indicators.note: stops means plugs a gap, so the illness goes inside the criminal

parts.note: a fence is a criminal who handles stolen goods
flu is an illness

explanation.surface: A crook's sickness halts his plan to get rich.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: affluence is riches, plenty of money.

clue.text: Antelope droppings turned up, first off

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up means read from the bottom upwards
first off says the opening letter of the droppings word is removed

parts.note: dung is animal droppings

explanation.surface: Antelope dung has been found, the first trace of the herd.
explanation.walkthrough: DUNG less its first letter is UNG, which 'turned up' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the wildebeest is a large African antelope.

clue.text: Woman gets sex, having affair

parts.note: she refers to a woman
bang is slang for sex

explanation.surface: A woman has sex while carrying on an extramarital fling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affair' suggests romance, but it means a business or matter, as in 'the whole shebang'.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal sense: the whole matter or set of things, as in 'the whole thing'.

clue.text: A cut might feel badly needed for this opera

indicators.note: badly says the letters are arranged poorly, so they need sorting into a new order

explanation.surface: An opera-goer imagines that one slash would sting terribly.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Mozart's Die Zauberflöte is an opera, known in English by this title.

clue.text: Medium-dry champagne initially abandoned as a failure

indicators.note: abandoned says a letter is given up from the word for medium-dry

parts.note: demi-sec is the term for medium-dry champagne or wine

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of champagne

explanation.surface: A sweetish fizz was dropped from the wine list because it flopped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Medium-dry champagne' looks like one phrase but splits: DEMI-SEC from the first part, then its C, from 'champagne initially', is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a downfall or end, as in the collapse of a company or plan.

clue.text: Violence in Turkey perhaps reported by quiet amateur

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so the word for a turkey is replaced by one that sounds the same

parts.note: a turkey is an example of fowl
p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
lay means non-professional, as in a lay preacher

explanation.surface: A news item about an amateur's quiet account of violence in Turkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turkey' with its capital suggests the country; it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: crime involving violence, especially murder, in detective stories.

clue.text: Review case of hunter happy to go shooting

indicators.note: to review is to look again, here taken as re-viewing the letters in a new order
case of takes the outside letters of hunter, its shell

explanation.surface: Assessing a hunting trip where the hunter was keen to go out shooting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shooting' suggests guns, but it is the camera sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Shooting is filming or taking pictures, the art of the camera.

clue.text: Supplier of claret wine and beer's home around five

parts.note: port is a fortified wine

indicators.note: around says the beer and home pieces sit on either side of the five

parts.note: ale is beer
V is the Roman numeral five
in means at home

explanation.surface: A list of a wine merchant's stock: claret, port and beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'claret' is old slang for blood, especially in boxing.
explanation.definitionFit: Anatomy: this vessel carries blood from the gut to the liver.

clue.text: Someone disabling networks? The deeds are his!

parts.note: LAN, local area network, is a computer network
a downer would be one who downs, puts out of action

explanation.surface: A saboteur crashing computer systems, gloating over his misdeeds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deeds' looks like actions, but means title deeds to property.
explanation.definitionFit: A property holder keeps the title documents to his estate.

clue.text: Bess's lover misses the first wild celebration

indicators.note: misses the first says the opening letter of the lover's name is dropped

parts.note: Porgy loves Bess in Gershwin's opera Porgy and Bess

explanation.surface: Bess's sweetheart fails to show up at the start of a wild party.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a riotous party or bout of indulgence.

clue.text: Cliff Richard album contains singles originally rejected

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the picked letters are read in reverse
originally picks the first letter of each of the four words before it

explanation.surface: A Cliff Richard LP includes tracks that were first turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cliff Richard' reads as the singer, but 'Cliff' is the definition and 'Richard' starts the run of initials RACS, which 'rejected' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a steep rock face, a crag.

clue.text: Be concerned about badger slaughter

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for be concerned goes round the badger word

parts.note: to care is to be concerned
to badger someone is to nag them

explanation.surface: Worry about the badger cull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badger' looks like the animal of the cull but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: mass killing, bloodshed on a large scale.

clue.text: Not a chap holding rank below duchess?

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the not-a-chap pieces wrap round the rest

parts.note: no means not a, as in 'no fool'
a man is a chap

indicators.note: rank as in offensive or gross suggests the letters are spoiled into a new order

explanation.surface: Asking whether an aristocratic woman, not a man, holds a rank lower than duchess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rank' looks like a title, but it is the anagram indicator (BLEWO); 'holding' is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a duchess is a lady of the peerage, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Aviator in a spot repressing rising anger

indicators.note: repressing means holding down inside, so the spot contains the anger

parts.note: a blot is a spot or stain

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the word for anger is read upwards

parts.note: ire is anger

explanation.surface: A flier stuck somewhere, suppressing his growing rage.
explanation.walkthrough: Louis Blériot was the French aviator who first flew the Channel, in 1909.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the French pioneer pilot of the first cross-Channel flight.

clue.text: State backed tabloid? That's the way into hell!

parts.note: to aver is to state firmly

indicators.note: backed means turned backwards, so the tabloid's name is reversed

parts.note: the Sun is a British tabloid newspaper

explanation.surface: A jibe that a tabloid backed by the state would be the road to damnation.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Classical myth: the lake near Naples said to be the entrance to the underworld.

clue.text: Fine wine including muscat regularly is sweet stuff

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

indicators.note: including means holding within, so the wine surrounds the picked letters

parts.note: rosé is a pink wine

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of muscat

explanation.surface: A wine-taster's note on a good wine with muscat in it being sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the even letters of muscat; 'including' puts them inside the wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Chemistry: fruit sugar, a naturally sweet compound.

clue.text: In retreat, forces rapidly cover a great distance

indicators.note: retreat means go back, so the hidden letters are read backwards
In says the letters sit inside the words forces rapidly

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Retreating troops move fast and cover a lot of ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft gave 'In retreat' to the reversal alone, leaving the hiding unsignalled; 'In' marks the hidden word and 'retreat' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronomy: a unit of length of about 3.26 light years, an immense span.

clue.text: Start to parley with a Chinese native

indicators.note: start to takes the first letter of parley

parts.note: and means with, together

explanation.surface: Opening talks with someone from China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chinese native' suggests a person, but it is an animal native to China.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the black-and-white bear found wild only in China.

clue.text: A short one contributes to new patient's getting restless after little time?

definitions.text: A short one contributes to new patient's getting restless after little time?

indicators.note: after says the shuffled letters come behind the little time

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time

indicators.note: contributes to means goes into, so the shortened one is put inside the shuffled letters
restless means unable to stay still, so all these letters are churned up together
short says the last letter of one is cut off

explanation.surface: A doctor's note: a fidgety new patient soon grows impatient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' makes ON, which 'contributes to' TENTISPAN (from 'getting restless' on N and PATIENTS); all comes 'after' T. Read whole, the clue says a short one leads to restlessness.
explanation.definitionFit: Psychology: how long someone can focus; a brief one leads to fidgeting and boredom.

clue.text: Nip round between times

indicators.note: between places the round inside the pair of times

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time, two of them for times
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Popping out quickly in a break between engagements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nip' looks like a verb, to pop out, but is the noun for a small drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a small measure of spirits, a dram.

clue.text: Harry Potter's first book for audio

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of Potter's
for audio means as heard, so the book's name is swapped for a word sounding the same

parts.note: Esther is a book of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: The first Harry Potter book released as an audiobook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' is the verb, to harass, not the boy wizard.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to harass or keep bothering someone.

clue.text: Fawning rubbish entertains one on day off

indicators.note: entertains means has as a guest, so the rubbish word holds the rest

parts.note: tosh is rubbish, nonsense

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the one follows the reworked day
off means gone bad, so the letters of day are spoiled into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Nonsense spoken to someone enjoying a day off, in the manner of a flatterer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' turns DAY into ADY; I goes 'on' it, and TOSH holds ADYI.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: grovelling and sycophantic, like a flatterer.
